text: The Heidel Taos is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Taos family, and is fought at level 38 at the Gotrock Oracle Ruins in Yesterdale during The Ouroboros Power.
The Happy Camper Gear is a Key Item in . It is obtained upon completing Elevator Repairs. It unlocks the ability to Cook and Craft Gems at rest spots.
Heartbreak Ignas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 44 at Raxeal Lavaflow on the Black Mountains.
Hallowcanter Hazerune (Japanese: , Teitetsu no Heizurūn) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Aries family, and can be found at level 42 at Belgazas' Drifts on the Black Mountains.
Hammurabi's Qmoeva (Japanese: , Hamurabi Sen'yō Kumūba) is a Tyrant in . It is a Qmoeva machine. It can be found at level 54 flying around the Tower of Eternity in Volitaris.

Ice Cabbages (Japanese: , Aisu Kyabetsu) are collectables in . They can be found on Valak Mountain. According to their description, they only grow in cold places and they look spicy but they are not. Two are needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 13,600 Noponstones.

Hill Fireflies (Japanese: , Zeppekihotaru) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, their behaviour is influenced by shooting stars. Four are required for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In the , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 2,400 Noponstones.

Ice Monkeys (Japanese: , Aisuaisezaru) are collectables in . They can be found on Valak Mountain. According to their description, they dwell in rock crevices in cold lands and their skin is smooth like ice.

Hox Flint is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can only be dropped by Porcu Hox in Valak Mountain or traded for via overtrading with Dakuku. According to their description, the slightest friction sets off a spark so one must be careful not to drop them. Three are needed for The Freezing Nopon.

The Hollow Bone (Japanese: , Kyoshin no Kanjō-kotsu, lit. Giant God's Annular Bone) is a landmark in . It is located on the upper level of Valak Mountain, in Bagnar Snowfield, on the northwest end of the map. Nopon Researchers can be found here. There is an ice slide in the cliff here that is presumably the Hollow Bone. It leads down to a small lake and then the Nopon Camp, with some more Nopon Researchers. Some quests are received both at the top and the bottom. If the party leader jumps at the right times on the slide, they will be able to access the Antol Den.

Homs Determination (Japanese: , Homusu no Iji) is a quest in . It can be received from Perrine in Colony 6. She can be found near the southern balcony around the center of Colony 6. This quest and Nopon Determination are mutually exclusive. Mechonis Core must be cleared and Odd Smoke - Resolution must have been completed. A 3-star affinity with Colony 6 is necessary to trigger this quest. If Riki is in the active party, he will comment. Accepting this quest causes a temporary loss of affinity with Colony 6 but recovered when the quest is completed, and a change in the Affinity Chart:

Hista Aries (Japanese: , Haisuta Ariesu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Aries family, and can be found at level 44 on Valak Mountain at night. Groups of them can be found around Ignia Hill, some accompanied by Zegia Ories. They can drop Frozen Aries Meat, two lots of which are needed for World's Strongest Flavour.

Hidden Gamigin (Japanese: , Inpei no Gamijin) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Taos family, and can be found at level 49 on Valak Mountain at night, on the natural bridge southeast of Ignia Hill.

Hovering Reef 9 (Japanese: , Dai 9 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It only connects to Hovering Reef 8. It has an island underneath it, like Hovering Reef 5, which has a large Wind Ether deposit of Pretty (rank III) crystals.

Hovering Reef 5 (Japanese: , Dai 5 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Hovering Reefs 4 and 6. The Flabbergasted Jerome can be found on the island located under this Hovering Reef, which must be defeated to complete Challenge.
Hovering Reef 7 (Japanese: , Dai 7 Fuyū Ganshō) is a location in . It is one of the Hovering Reefs, and is located above Eryth Sea. It connects to Hovering Reef 4 and Central Seal Island.

Hidden Thorn (Japanese: , Haido Supaiku, Hide Spike) is one of Fiora's early game physical arts in . It inflicts damage, and also inflicts Daze if used on a Toppled enemy. Damage is calculated based on the weapon's attack + Fiora's strength.

House of Cards is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Yardley and the primary destination is the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. Completing this mission will result in the discovery of the Yardley's Hideaway landmark. It also unlocks the ability to use Yardley's machine to change Cross's appearance, gender and voice by taking them back to the character creation screen; however the machine can only be used late at night (0:00 – 04:59) when Yardley is present.

Hit Rate, also called Accuracy, is a game mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is the probability of an attack hitting its target. The Hit Rate for physical attacks (including Auto-Attacks) is based on Agility, Level, armour weight, and tension. The Hit Rate for ether attacks is similar, but ignores agility and armour weight, and the level difference modifier is more moderate. Holy Lancer Efrain (Japanese: , Seisō no Asupidokeron) is a Unique Monster in . He is a member of the Marrin family and can be found at level 51 in the Chamber of Pillars of Spirit Crucible Elpys. He rises from the abyss slowly when the player approaches, but slowly enough that the player may very well run past without even noticing him. He must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 4 "Greatest Warrior" and Agate's level 5 Star Beryl Courage on their Affinity Charts. Holy Lancer Efrain is immune to Break.
Hot Moonbeam Salads are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be created by Pyra at the kitchens in Tora's House and Corinne's House.
Hide 'n' Creepers are Tree collectibles in . They can be found in the Leftherian Archipelago, in particular in the east side of the Ansel Hatchery island.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Holy Necklaces (Japanese: , Seijo no Kubikazari) are accessories in . They increase the rate of healing of Recovery-type Arts by up to 24%, boosting their healing power. They are the upgraded version of the Harvest Necklace and Affection Necklace accessories. The DLC exclusive Saint's Necklace accessory offers a stronger instance of this equipment's effect.
History Teacher is a quest in . It can be received from Willas on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Hot Nopon is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Ice Mastery", "Fire Mastery" and "Birdbrain" Field Skills.

Ice Hunter is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal by talking to Stidias at Theoscaldia Palace, when the nation has at least 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Passionate Soul", "Wind Mastery" and "Earth Mastery" Field Skills.

Hototo is an NPC in . He is a Nopon found in the Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya, where he manages the supplies. He is the father of Kikina who has a lot of respect for his father and the work the mercs do. Hototo can be first found in the Fusty Fungus Caves. He at one point spotted Zeke outside Garfont Village and mistook him for a hooded Igna Driver who was plotting to destroy the village with his "Eye of Shining Justice". The party never revealed to Hototo that said Igna was actually Zeke, who poses no threat to Garfont.

Hot Spring Bonanza is a DLC Quest in . It is part of the New Quests Pack 4 of the Expansion Pass. It can be accepted after completing Chapter 10 by speaking to Gachagacha at the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild and giving him 100 Gold with Kasandra, Kora, and Sheba in the party. Kasandra's One Lucky Gal Lv3 Field Skill is required to receive the quest.

Hurryscurry is a Nopon in . He is added in the version 1.5.1 update. He can be found at the Bower Lounge in the Argentum Trade Guild after A Firecracker of a Gal is collected and the ability to awaken Blades is unlocked. He is a courier who delivers the Ebullient Core Crystal to the party, after which he makes his leave.

Hyber Village (Japanese: , Haiberu no Mura) is a landmark in . It is a tiny village located on the west side of the upper level of the Aletta Region of the Kingdom of Torna, just beyond Olnard's Trail. There are several green barrels containing Red Pollen Orbs here, and various Collection Points. The quest For Lack of a Hunter can be accepted here, and MacNeth can be found here during Duplicity. The Navy-Blue Slate Piece can be found in one of the abandoned houses. There are no enemies in the village itself, but there are several in the unnamed area between the village and The Braying Canyon. These are listed below.
Hover Stones are three Key Items in . Each one is found at Soltnar Seal Island, Pillar Knoll, and Scapular Lance, and are required for Rubble Trouble.

Highly-Piley Ocean's Bounties are Meal items in . They can be cooked by Manana at Rest Spots. One Silver Nopon Coin can be used to cook this meal instead of the necessary ingredients. It is unlocked by purchasing the Erythia Sashimi Plate from the Station Breakroom for the first time.
Icicle Marines are Gemstone collectibles in . They can be found on the Black Mountains.
Highpike Tirkins are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 42 on the Black Mountains.

How the Future Endures is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track ten of disc eight from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track ten of disc nineteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays when N and M sacrifice themselves to destroy Z for good.

Inferno Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Inferno Heinrich and Cratere Nebulae on Prison Island. According to their description, they are fire elements that create 300 degree flames in just three seconds. Two are required for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 11,000 Noponstones.

Insanity Mints (Japanese: , Kurēji Minto, Crazy Mint) are collectables in . They can be found in Tephra Cave and later in Colony 6. According to their description, they emit a smell powerful enough to knock someone out. Three are needed for one route of Overworked and Underpaid.

Insanity Mosses (Japanese: , Maddo Mosu, Mad Moss) are collectables in . They can be found in Prison Island. According to their description, they are an ochre moss that does not wither and touching them causes someone to feel sick.

The Imperial Villa (Japanese: 離宮, Rikyū) is a landmark in . It is located on the second floor of Alcamoth and can be reached from the teleporter in the north wing of the Great Hall. Melia lives here and mentions that her deceased mother, the un-named Homs second consort, loved the place. The Heart-to-Heart, "Melia's Imperial Villa", is located here. After the events at Mechonis Core, it becomes inhabited by two Aora Telethia and five Arel Telethia. During A Release From Duty, Telethia Galdo can be found here, standing alone within the villa itself, in the north of the area. In the , a Time Attack Portal can be found here.

Inferno Deinoses (Japanese: , Karoru Dinosu) are enemies in . They are members of the Deinos family, and can be found from level 31-35 near the Eks Watering Hole. Inferno Deinoses have a small frill of fire on the back of their heads. Defeating five of them is required to complete Lousy Lizards given by Modamo in Frontier Village. In addition, they can drop the Peachy Leg Joints needed for Leku's Food Crisis and the Magic Stones needed for Material Quest 1.

Invited Slobos (Japanese: , Shōrai no Sorobosu) is a quest-exclusive enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Slobos family, and can be found at level 99 at Three Sage Summit on Valak Mountain. It appears once the quest The Final Giants' Ruins is completed by reaching the Giant's ruins, it is not required to defeat it. The Invited Slobos is amongst the rare quest-exclusive enemies that respawn after the quest is completed, along with the Woeful Upas. It will drop the Slobos Ice Rocks needed for En Argentis' Betrothal Test.

Inferno Heinrich (Japanese: , Entei no Hainrihi) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 76 in the back of the Kitchen in Prison Island. It is slightly larger than the surrounding Cratere Nebulae. It can drop the Inferno Elements needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Illustrious Golteus (Japanese: , Ōzora no Goruteusu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Pterix family and can be found at level 98, flying around the Precipice Bridge in Makna Forest after the Mechonis Core events.

In Ose Tower (Japanese: , Ose no Tō nite) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Sealed Tower on Valak Mountain, between Riki and Dunban at green affinity.

Irina Akulov (Japanese: , Irina Akurofu; English dub: ) is one of the eight main playable characters of . She is a team leader within the Interceptors Division, and a member of BLADE. Irina becomes recruitable after Chapter 3. Before Earth was destroyed, she was a part of the Unified Government Forces Special Vehicle Guidance Squad as Elma's subordinate. She idolizes and respects Elma, having previously worked under her. She has a strong desire to protect the people of Mira.

Immortal Ictuses (Japanese: , Imōtaru Manda) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ictus family. They can be found at level 55 at Roof Rock, Talon Rock Third Terrane, East Gate Plain, and North Janpath Plain, or at level 60 near Grieving Plains in Primordia at night.

Island Saltats (Japanese: , Airando Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 11-12 or at level 16-17 in Cauldros on a shore northwest of FN Site 505 during clear weather.

Inferno Ictuses (Japanese: , Inferuno Manda) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ictus family, and can be found at level 49 in Primordia, north of Roof Rock or North Janpath Plain during the night, or Talon Rock Third Terrane (some only appear during the day). Defeating three of them is required to complete the basic mission Ictus Infestation (5 stars).

Idyll Beach (Japanese: , Mahorahama) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a very small beach located at the FN Site 223 in Noctilum. It can be found by swimming along the eastern side of the northern island of Noctilum. Like all Unexplored Territories, its discovery yields an achievement ("The Heavenly Idyll Beach"). Unlike most other areas outwith New Los Angeles the Idyll Beach shows signs of Human activity already, as a pair of deck chairs and beach umbrella have been set up. There are no enemies here.

The Infantry Support Qmoeva (Japanese: , Hohei Shien-gata Kumūba) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Qmoeva Ganglion's skell. It can be found at level 80 on a small island in the north westernmost corner of Noctilum Waters.

It's-a Mia! (Japanese: , Mīa no Hishō, Mia's Flight) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Mia near the Cleansing Spring in Sylvalum. It is the fourth of five Missions that culminate in Mia being able to be recruited.

In a Jam is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Dodonga Caravan and the primary destination is Primordia. It requires the party to obtain a sample of jelly weeds, which can be found on the smallest of a set of three islands in the sky above Primordia's northern coast.

The Indoline Praetorium (Japanese: , Ākedia Hōōchō, lit. Acēdia Holy See/Episcopal Government) is a Nation in . It is the theocratic government of the Titan Indol. Its people worship the Titans. This organization has influence on military, it controls the procurement and supply of Core Crystals, of which Blades are born, and keeps every Blade in Alrest officially tracked and controlled. The Praetorium on Indol is a traditional religious state with a beautiful cityscape. The Praetor is also the ruler of the people on the Titan. Indol is home to many refugees from various dying Titans and wars. The Indoline Praetorium is where the Blade Eater technology was born. When the party reaches the Sky

The Indoline are a race in and . They live on the Titan Indol where they have built a Praetorium nation in which they can mainly be found, though they trace their origins to the now-destroyed nation of Judicium, in the Titan Temperantia. They are tall, slender human-like people with blue skin and pointed ears, and have extremely long lifespans compared to other races.

The Isle of Urchon (Japanese: , Unin-jima) is a location in . It is located in the Fonsett Waters in the Leftherian Archipelago, between Ysheva Harbor and Godsford Isle. A small unnamed island nearby can be reached by jumping onto one of the small moving Titans, which passes between the Urchon and Godsford Isles. It has a Treasure Trove containing a Pouch Expansion Kit and a small amount of Gold. The Heart-to-Heart "Free as a Bird" is located here, as is a Salvage Point.

The Island Base Lindwurm (Japanese: , Guntō - Rintovurumu) is a location in . It is located in Fonsett Waters in the Leftherian Archipelago. It acts as the main headquarters of the terrorist organization Lindwurm, with the Red Room underground functioning as a saferoom. It can be reached by going to Godsford Isle, going to the north end of the Isle, and then proceeding down the path. The Red Room may be accessed after acquiring the Basement Key during Bana's Revenge.

Incandescent Marcus (Japanese: , Shakunetsu no Joruto) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Plambus family, and can be found at level 54 at the top of the Pillar City Ruins in the Kingdom of Tantal, reachable from the top by Skip Travelling from the Airborne Throne, or from the bottom by building an ice bridge.

The Indoline Loyalist (Japanese: , Ākedia Rāgen) is a boss in . He is an Indoline guard who is fought at level 57 at the 7th Perimeter Center Floor in the World Tree. He is accompanied by the Indoline Star. This enemy drops no items.

Illegal Dumper is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and is unlocked automatically when the Garfont Mercenaries reach Merc Level 5 and the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 80 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 20 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Industry Mastery" and "Electric Mastery" Field Skills.

Insect Professor is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Indoline Praetorium from Doridd near the Refugee Campground, when the nation has at least 2 stars in Development Level. After Chapter 8, it can also be received automatically from the Leftherian Archipelago; if the mission was already unlocked in Indol before that point, it will be transferred to Leftheria. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector" and "Forestry" Field Skills.
Into the Open Sky is a quest in . It can be received from Panpan on Argentum's Goldmouth Flight Deck.

Ilmina is an NPC in . She can be found at the Cargo Transportation Zone in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the day. She offers the Merc Mission Volff Tricks. She is a kind, older woman who still works with Ardainian exports and cargo to ship internationally. Ilmina woefully comments on how though Mor Ardain is able to produce many goods related to tech, almost all food on the Titan is imported from other nations. She also tells the player to hurry to the city since "you probably don't want to hang around in a dusty old place like this."

Impregnable Sandhu (Japanese: , Nankōfuraku no Jinguu) is a Unique Monster in . They are an Agnus Soldier, and can be found at level 82 at the Ruins of Seebu in the Urayan Tunnels. They form the "Agnian Assassins" duo with Godlike Krastor. The Fiery Morale Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating them.
Island Bunnits are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 44-48 at Migrow's Rosary in Erythia Sea.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Incense of Elegance are Accessories in and . In , The common variant can be purchased from the Battlescar Caravan, and the legendary variant can be obtained from Spiky Aurelia. In , the common variant can be purchased from the Colony 9 Supply Office for 7800 G, and the legendary variant can be obtained from a Relic in the Black Mountains near The Alabaster Throne.
Inferno Dance is a Battle Art in . It is one of the arts of the Seraph class. The user hops at the enemy and does a powerful fire slash with their lance while also taking damage themselves.
Iguaz Symbols are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Standard family, and can be found at level 44 at Raxeal Lavaflow on the Black Mountains. They drop rare Symbol Ornaments.

Igruna Standards are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are stationary Standard enemies that alert nearby Ignas when attacked. They can be found at level 44 in the Igna territory at the Argan Cathedral Ruins on the Black Mountains. They drop rare Standard Decorations.
Ignia Hill (Japanese: , Iginia-zaka) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of Valak Mountain, and two Unique Monsters, the Agile Barbatos and the Hidden Gamigin, can be found near it.
Journey's End (Japanese: , Nagai Tabi no Hate ni) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Empty Throne on Prison Island, between Riki and Reyn at pink affinity.

The Junks Deck is a landmark in . It is located on the flying Junks when it is temporarily an area, after the events at the Mechonis Core while escaping the destruction of Mechonis. After the story event involving the Telethia attack of the Junks, this landmark is unveiled when the battle against the Sureny Telethia starts, and the deck serves as this boss battleground fenced by a green field barrier.
Jaculs (Japanese: , Hasutara) are flying bird-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are counterparts of the Auravis.
Keegan Ridge (Japanese: , Kebin Sanchi, Kevin Mountains) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, east of Aaroy Plain and south of King's Falls.

Katerina, the Cliffhanger (Japanese: , Dangai no Katerīna) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Mortifole family. It can be found hidden at level 48 on a small island south of Everwhelm Falls in Noctilum.

Jaharmums (Japanese: , Jaharumamu) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros, in particular around Titan's Table or on the waters to the southeast of the continent. Seven are needed for BLADE Mission No. 16's Squad Task.

Jia Mian, the Beloved (, Saiai no Jiamien) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Jacul family. It can be found at level 50 northeast of Mount M'gando in Cauldros, flying above a strange structure. The Storm Jaculs in the nearby basket-like structure will aggro if Jia Mian is attacked, and vice versa. It must be defeated for Squad Mission No.17.

Joker, the Unknowable (Japanese: , Hiō no Jōkā) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is the strongest member of the Blatta family. It can be found at level 90 at Divine Roost in Noctilum inside the giant tree, which can be entered from the treetop with the Flight Module. It is a major source of level 60 gear. Killing it is required for segment recon.

The Jacul Rage (Japanese: , Hasutara Gurāji, Jocul Grudge) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Jacul family, and is fought at level 43 at the Lower Delusian Mountains in Sylvalum during The Duel (Part III).

Jagron's Citadel (Japanese: , Jagāru no Nejiro) is a location in . It is located on the Central Plain of Temperantia, along a passage south west of Toxbloom Spring. There is a buried Treasure Trove here containing several Shining Star Chips and a Legendary Core Crystal, unearthing it requires the level 2 "Fortitude" and level 4 "Earth Mastery" Field Skills.

Jewel Krabbles (Japanese: , Jueru Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family and can be found at level 36-43 on the Upper Level - Right area of the Gormott Province, particularly on Lascham Island or at Varnax's Plunge.
Jaruru is a Nopon NPC in . He can be found in the Old City of Teddim in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

The Juppen Krabble (Japanese: , Jupen Kuraibu) is a Story and Quest Exclusive Enemy in . It is a member of the Krabble family and is fought at level 9 at Lascham Island on the Upper Level - Right of the Gormott Province during Artificial Blade Parts 2.

The Key-Shaped Lever is a Key Item in . It is obtained by Salvaging on the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild. It is one of the three key items needed to open the chest in the quest Bana's Secret Treasure.

Juicy Ray Fins are Enemy Part collectibles in . They can be dropped by Manda Moramoras. For unknown reasons, they can also drop from Sarta Garluses. They are one of several items which can be used to satisfy one of the objectives in Fly in the Ointment.

Jenth Garluses (Japanese: , Tsento Garuusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Garlus family and can be found at level 37 - 43 at Pillar City Ruins on the Upper Level of Kingdom of Tantal. They can be fought at level 103 during the Challenge Battle, Humanoid Alliance.

The Judicium Titans, or Aeshmas, are medium sized Titans in . These Titans have been weaponized with the technology of the ancient Judicium nation in Temperantia, which was destroyed during the Aegis War. When encountered by the party, an activated Titan is controlled by Jin.
Kastina is an NPC in . She is a Tantalese who can be found sitting on a bench at Elmos Square in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. She is involved during the Quest Fly in the Ointment.

Jubel Feris (Japanese: , Yūberu Ferisu) are story exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Feris family, and can be found at level 2 in Lasaria Woodland in the Kingdom of Torna. Alongside several Raging Volffs and Cursed Buloofo, they are the first enemies in the game. As with all story exclusive enemies in , this enemy drops no items, only gold. For some reason, these specific Feris possess a powerful version of the Art "Plunging Fang" which has a damage ratio of 1,800. For comparison, Artifice Aion's "Prometheus" art has a damage ratio of 2,000.

Karifo Gyaarks are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Gyaark family, and can be found at level 45-46 at Erythia Sea. One is also fought at level 53 during the fourth wave of the Challenge Battle Ocean Day Parade.

K's Portrait is a Key Item in . It is a portrait of Consul K painted by Stefaan. He gives it to the party during An Artist. According to Wellwell, it is worth 200,000 G. The party can sell the painting to him after the quest is completed. The painting can then be found displayed in the City's Medical Facility.
Joulietta (Japanese: , Jurietta) is an NPC in who can be found in the City. She is a member of House Doyle and the daughter of Garrett.
Jaggar (Japanese: , Jougo) is an NPC in who can be found in the City.

Jake is a NPC in . He is a member of the Lost Numbers who is found at the Memorial Hall in the City after the DLC Quest For the Sake of Keepsakes. He and Tessa are married and have been very close for years.

Janus is an NPC in . He is a City Survivor who is initially found near the Waypoint Sapling on the Aurora Shelf. After being rescued, he can be found around Colony 9's Command Center in Yesterdale. Janus's Community is gained when talking to him after completing the quest Instructor Panacea, completing Chapter 3, and then talking with him four times.

Jump Towards the Morning Sun is a track from , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. Joanne Hogg is a Northern Irish musician, and lead singer and songwriter of the Celtic band named Iona. She is the vocalist for Future Awaits, from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack. She also gave her vocals for Tetsuya Takahashi's previous works: Small Two of Pieces and Stars of Tears from Xenogears, as well as Pain and Kokoro from Xenosaga Episode I: Der Wille zur Macht.

Kurralth (Japanese: , Kuraru) is a High Entia in . He is an adventurer, and often goes on journeys with his partner, Zain. He can be found to the northeast of the Fountain of Eternity in Alcamoth, by the escalator, with Zain. After the events at the Mechonis Core, he can be found in Harict Chapel on Valak Mountain. If Adventurers in Peril was not completed, Kurralth (who is in the Chapel) must be spoken to, and he sends the party to find Zain near Three Sage Summit.

Large Handcuffs (Japanese: , Kyojū Handokafu, Large Beast Handcuffs) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found on Valak Mountain. They are made of green monster fur and it did not take long for Reyn to name them.

Lacus Swamp (Japanese: , Rakusu-numa) is a location in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, on the northwest portion of the map, south of Kelsher Wetland, the entrance from Colony 6. On an island in the middle of the swamp is the Nopon Merchant Camp, where some Nopon Merchants are found and some quests are given.

Lampo Ponios are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Ponio family, and can be found at level 54 around the Giant Mechon Debris on the Fallen Arm at daytime. Four of them must be defeated to complete Powerless. They are the only enemies that can drop the Ponio Hoof Seals needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Kromars (Japanese: , Supikaru) are an enemy family in and . They are bipedal reptilian enemies. Kromars are exclusively found at Eryth Sea with the exception of the Brutal Gravar, found in King Agni's Tomb in Makna Forest. Kromars are similar in appearance and may be related to Ignas and Merignas. The most powerful Kromar is the Stormy Belagon, at level 87. The behaviour, adornments and social structure of Kromars strongly suggest they are an intelligent race, but they can still be harmed by the Monado unlike the Homs, Nopon and High Entia.
The Kitchen (Japanese: , Chūbō) is a location in . It is located on the first floor of Prison Island. It is locked at first, but can be unlocked by obtaining the Kitchen Door Key in the Arena.

Latael Shore (Japanese: , Rataeru Kaigan) is a landmark in . It the first location in Eryth Sea, the destination reached from Frontier Village, however the party cannot travel back to the village from here. It is inhabited by Cruz Paguls and Lunar Gradies, with several Perna Elucas on the higher grassy area. There is usually a Nebula of some sort down the west end of the beach, depending on the weather. After Mechonis Core, a single Arel Telethia is also present here. The beach's only exit is a teleporter to Hovering Reef 1, although the party can swim from it.

La Luz Church (Japanese: , Ra Rūsu kyōkai) is a landmark in . It is a temple of High Entia origin within the lower section of Valak Mountain. The entrance is up on the ledge south of the Sealed Tower, and can only be accessed from a cave under the church, by climbing up from it. The cave entrance is southeast of the church entrance on the ledge, in the lighter-shaded area of the map.

Kyel Lexos are enemies in . They are members of the Lexos family, and can be found from level 70-72 on the Freight Road of Colony 6 when it is raining. They do not appear until after the final battle at Mechonis Core. Along with the Unreliable Rezno, they drop the Ocean Elixir of Life required for Replica Monado 2 and Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Laia (Japanese: , Raia) are a family of flying enemies in the . Some members of the family are known as Skyrays (Japanese: , An'noun, Unknown). This species is close to Moramora. Two varieties appear in , although only the black variety appears in . While Laias appear in , only Moramoras appear in , with fossilized Laia being obtainable as collectibles.

Latio Apis (Japanese: , Ratio Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Apis family, and can be found at level 41 on Valak Mountain in the Apis Lair. They can drop Apis Gold Nuggets, which are required for Material Quest 3.

Krawli Slobos (Japanese: , Kurouri Sorobosu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Slobos family and can be found at level 46 during the day near Nofol Tower on Valak Mountain. They can drop the Slobos Ice Rocks needed for En Argentis' Betrothal Test.

Krawla Slobos (Japanese: , Kuroura Sorobosu) are enemies in . They are members of the Slobos family, and can be found at level 47 at night near Nofol Tower on Valak Mountain. They can drop the Slobos Ice Rocks needed for En Argentis' Betrothal Test.

The Kitchen Door Key is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found in the hallway south of the Arena in Prison Island. The Bone Pillar must be raised to be able to pick up this item. Afterwards it can be used to unlock the door in the southern half of the wall between the Banquet Hall and the Kitchen, enabling the party to revisit the Kitchen, the Bone Pillar controls, and the Behemoth Nest.

Laia Intestines are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Masterful Gigapur or Newgate Laias on Prison Island. Laia Intestines are not otherwise available. According to their description, they contain an acid that can dissolve anything but themselves.

Lacerate (Japanese: , Deddorī Baito, Deadly Bite) is one of Fiora's early game physical arts in . Fiora swings her knives upward, inflicting Bleed on an enemy. Damage is calculated based on the weapon's attack + Fiora's strength.

Land Forfexes (Japanese: , Rando Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 21-27 near Barbarich Desert, FN Site 319, around Great Washington Isle, in the oasis north of Rooney Cavern, and at South Coast in Oblivia. They usually burrow out from the ground upon spawning. White Forfex Shells will be dropped if the head is targeted and destroyed.

Lake Basel (Japanese: , Bāzeru-ko) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a massive lake located in northeastern Oblivia. Dorian Caravan is located on an island in the lake, the Floating Reef is in the sky directly above and the FN Site 316 is on the northwestern shore. The lake must be visited during Unknown Assailant, and the Mimeosome Right Leg can be found on the northwest shore after Arms and the Man. Lan'cord can be found here during Securing Lan'cord.

Kiweggs (Japanese: , Egguui) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular the northeast part around Dorian Caravan where Lake Basel turns into a waterfall at the top and the small island to the right of that. Alternatively, they can be found atop King's Falls. Fourteen of them are needed for route A of the Normal Mission The Trading Floor.
Kridokan Airs (Japanese: , Kuridokaro no Kūki) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia's cave areas, as well as in the mountainous region of Ibra Ravine.

L-002 Degeneration Reactors (Japanese: , L-002 Shukutairo Star-buck) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular near Oblivia Ingress, Jair Fortress, and the north-eastern Oblivia Waters.
L-002 Power Cables are Important Items in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Three are needed during The Repair Job, they can be found in Primordia's Starfall Basin.

Kw'arah Villa (Japanese: , Ku-Ara Rikyū) is a landmark in . It is located in Cauldros. The building is a massive superstructure and cannot be entered, though its rooftop can be traversed by a Skell with a Flight Module, or in the by gliding through the air with a Hraesvelg from the southernmost terminus of the elevated walkway leading south from the western flank of Mount M'gando. Kw'arah Villa has a virtually identical exterior and dimensions as G'nahan Villa, also in Cauldros. There are no enemies here during normal gameplay, but a pair of Orion Xern hover close by and above.

Lastyr Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Grenada Galactic Group Raygun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Natural Artifacts category of the Noctilum Collectopedia. The Lastyr weapons available in-game are: * Storm Lastyr * Soldier Lastyr * Warrior Lastyr * Ophidian Lastyr * Destroyer Lastyr * Striker Lastyr * Delta Lastyr * Cosmic Lastyr * Nebulan Lastyr

Lastyr II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Grenada Galactic Group Raygun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Relics category of the Cauldros Collectopedia. Lastyr III Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Grenada Galactic Group Raygun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Unknown Assailant, alongside the Parma II Series. The Lastyr III weapons available in-game are: * Storm Lastyr III * Soldier Lastyr III * Warrior Lastyr III * Ophidian Lastyr III * Destroyer Lastyr III * Striker Lastyr III * Delta Lastyr III * Cosmic Lastyr III * Nebulan Lastyr III

Lance Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Six Stars Javelin. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Queen Is Dead. The Lance weapons available in-game are: * Audacious Lance * Faithful Lance * Intrepid Lance * Masterstroke Lance * Pulverizing Lance * Steelbreaker Lance * Godbreaker Lance * Phenomenon Lance

Like Uraya, the Titan swims beneath the Cloud Sea and everything lives inside it. Its climate is far colder than other Titans and is the only Titan seen with snowfall. Khulkhan is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian who can be found during the day on the right side of the Goldmouth Flight Deck in the Argentum Trade Guild. He offers the Merc Mission Unloading of Goods. His job is making deliveries, and he mentions always appreciating any help he can get with them from mercenaries, calling it "Better than them lazing around".
The Laplas Driver (Japanese: , Rapurasu Doraibā) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . He is a Driver enemy fought at level 36 on the Training Ground in the Kingdom of Uraya during A Test of Strength.

King of the Spring is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya by talking to Remmiq behind the Harghalgh Inn, when the nation has at least 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Water Mastery", "Fortitude" and "Ichthyology" Field Skills.
Kingdom Destroyer is an Info Item in . It can be obtained after completing the Merc Mission The Beast of Regideria. It is used during the quest Lost Kingdom.

The Lasaria Region (Japanese: , Risaria Chihō) of the Kingdom of Torna is the first area visited in . It is located in the Southwest part of Torna. The Lasaria Region is the only region of Torna that doesn't connect with the other regions of the Titan. However, it is possible to see some destroyed stairs in Feltley Village that lead towards the Loftin Nature Preserve in the Dannagh Region.

The Lascham Peninsula (Japanese: , Rasukamu Hantō) is a location in . It is a small island located in the southwestern area of Gormott, just east of and down the hill from Lascham Cove. There is a Treasure Trove and an ether miasma here.

Killhappy Brijaidor (Japanese: , Kyoetsu no Burigeidā) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Merfrey family, and can be found at level 79 at the northern side of Vinisog Holm and behind the Vinisog Holm Camp in Erythia Sea. The Strength Support Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
Krammit Device Fragments are items in . One of yellow rarity is needed to craft a level 3 Empowered Combo gem.
Kio is an NPC and in who can be found in Colony 15, and later in the City.
Kotan is an NPC in who can be found in the City. He is the twin brother of Taleb.
Kisame (Japanese: ) is a character in who can be found on Vinisog Holm. She eventually moves back to the City.

Lightning Weasels (Japanese: , Inazumaitachi) are collectables in . They can be found in Prison Island and Colony 6. According to their description, they are cute little blue-eyed weasels that can move at lightning speed.

Lexos Dragon Elixirs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. One is dropped by the story quest exclusive Conflagrant Raxeal on Valak Mountain during the story quest The Magma Rock, others can be obtained through Riki's Yoink!. There is no other method to obtain them as no one has them for trade. According to their description, they illuminate the inside of the mouth and are considered a delicious assault on the senses.

Lightning Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Saldox Nebulae on Prison Island or traded for with Don Argentis in Alcamoth before he migrates to Colony 6. According to their description, they are lightning elements that bring down a thunderbolt 8 seconds after they are buried.
Levitaths (Japanese: , Rukiora) are gigantic whale-like flying Insectoid enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, Noctilum, and Oblivia.

Lazuli Forfexes (Japanese: , Razūri Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 61-64 on an island in Sylvalum Waters, northwest of FN Site 404.

Lea Lilies (Japanese: , Ria Suzuran) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, in particular the mountainous parts of the region. Six are needed for the basic mission Lilting Lilies.
Lepyx Moonstones are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Lepyxes' bodies or back appendages in Sylvalum. They are required for Potential Up augments.

Launchers Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Sakuraba Industries Psycho Launchers. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Insects category of the Oblivia Collectopedia. Ligar Rhoguls (Japanese: , Rigāru Rōguru) are enemies in . They are members of the Rhogul family and can be found at level 16 - 19 flying above various locations on the Upper Level of the Gormott Province when it is not raining.

Leftherian Murals is an Info Item in . It hints at the location of the Mysterious Part D. It can be obtained by examining the mural to the west of Corinne's House on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago. The level 3 "Keen Eye" and "Ancient Wisdom" Field Skills are required to be able to read the mural.

Levma Bunnits (Japanese: , Revuma Banitto) are enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 32 - 36 at the Baldotas Isle in the Leftherian Archipelago. Four of them must be defeated to unlock Poppibuster's level 2 "Superstrength" Field Skill.

Lifesaving (Japanese: , Jinmeikyūjo) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the Garfont Mercenaries reach Merc Level 5 and the nation reaches 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Industry Mastery", "Lockpicking" and "Info Collector" Field Skills.

Lavean is a High Entia in . He can initially be found at Xen's Thoroughfare on the Bionis' Shoulder. When first spoken to, he mentions that his brother is missing and that the Somnivore Lexos was his sworn enemy. Upon defeating the Lexos on Soltnar Seal Island, a Faded ID Tag belonging to the missing brother is acquired. After a story-required visit to Alcamoth, Lavean offers the quest Brother's Keepsake if shown the Faded ID Tag. After completion of his quest, Lavean can be found paying his respects to his departed brother at Heroes' Rest.

Levialord Empireo (Japanese: , Hakairyū Enpireo, Supreme Sea Dragon Empireo) is a Superboss in . It is a Unique Monster and a member of the Ravoon family, and can be found at level 110 in The Aegis Sea in Erythia Sea. The Power Pick-Me-Up Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating it. Through re-challenging, Levialord Empireo's level can be increased to a maximum at level 180.

Lieselotte is an NPC in . She is a Tantalese who can be found in Elmos Square in the Kingdom of Tantal during Fly in the Ointment.

Lunara (Japanese: , Ruru) is a young High Entia in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found waiting at the bottom of the main escalator at night, directly to the east of the Main Entrance in Alcamoth. When first encountered following the events on Prison Island, she frets that her father has not returned home after the battle with the Mechon and fears it is because he does not love her. In Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition, Lunara's English dialogue is changed. She remains worried that her father has not come home, but also notes that her father would show his affection with cuddles. She does not state any worry regarding her father's love for her.

Lucky Chilkin Rings are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Bow Chilkins on Valak Mountain, and are not available for trade. According to their description, they are rings from the fairy tale 'Tin-Tiki-Tin' although they are totally worthless. Two are needed to complete Betrothal Test involving Zel Argentis and given by Oleksiy in Colony 6.

M35 Prototypes (Japanese: , Sanjūgoshiki: PROTO) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Mechon, and can be found at level 54 to the south of the Hidden Machina Village and to the west of the Giant Mechon Debris on the Fallen Arm. Four of them must defeated to complete Powerless. They are the only source of the Dated Plugs needed for Odd Smoke - Resolution.

Lograt Kromars (Japanese: , Rogorato Supikaru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Kromar family, and can be found at level 86 at the Eryth Sea, on Kromar Coast and the Secluded Island.

Lophos Moramoras (Japanese: , Roposu Moramora) are enemies in . They are members of the Moramora family, and can be found at level 44 at night in various areas on Valak Mountain, including just below Zokhed Pass and near Nagul Waterfall. They drop Moramora Meat Pies, three of which are needed for the quest Reversed Tastes.

Long Barg Ears are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained only from the Bargs in Prison Island. Long Barg Ears are not otherwise available. According to their description, they can hear what the heart says and anyone who does not think so should hold it to someone's heart and see for themselves.

Little Suids (Japanese: , Ritoru Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family. They are smaller than Brass Suids and Brass Femina Suids. They can be found at level 1-50 throughout Primordia, typically in the presence of adult suids. Five must be defeated to complete one route of City Saviors. They can drop the Suid Fillet needed for Suid Sirloin.

Lord Xe-dom (Japanese: , Rōdo Ze-raa) is an enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Xe-dom family. Lord Xe-dom can be found at level 65 on floating islands west of Talon Rock Summit or directly above FN Site 108 in Primordia.
Little Caro (Japanese: , Ritoru Nokkusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Caro and can be found at level 36-37 at the Lower Delusian Mountains in Sylvalum.
Lower Delusian Mountains (Japanese: , Meimōsan no Kasō) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, south of the North Silent Sandsea. It is home to a large pack of Caro.

Lovely Pom Poms are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are obtained from different species of Ovis after destroying their posterior appendage. They are required for Resist Knockback and Resist.KNOCKBACK augments.

Lutetia Petramands (Japanese: , Ruteshia Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family and can be found at level 53-55 at FN Site 404 and the bottom of the Delusian Mountains southeast of FN Site 419 in Sylvalum.

Lutetium Petramands (Japanese: , Rutechiumu Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family and can be found at level 51-53 in the lava river near the Ruined City of O'rrh Sim in Cauldros.
Luxaar's Xern (Japanese: , Rukuzāru Sen'yō Zerun) is a Tyrant in and . It is the Xern aircraft of Luxaar. It can be found at level 90 in Sylvalum, flying above Anvil Sandplain.

Lugalbanda, the Wanderer-King (Japanese: , Hōrō-ō Rugarubanda) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Chimera family. It can be found at level 88 at the Vitriol Cesspool in Noctilum after completing Chapter 12. This location is inaccessible to Skells, so Lugalbanda must be fought on foot. It can summon Stray Ovis for assistance by using an Art called "Lunchtime". This monster is notable for dropping the very powerful Longsword, Bewitched Glaive: Receding Rust. During battles with Lugalbanda, the Wanderer-King, the boss theme "CR17S19S8" plays instead of the standard Tyrant theme "Uncontrollable".

Lofty Aetrygons (Japanese: , Ea Derupinu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Aetrygon family, and can be found at level 41-46 in the sky around the large mountain between Cavernous Abyss and Xanadu Overlook in Sylvalum.
M-Lasers are back weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Qmoevas bosses or by destroying Qmoevas' weapon appendages.
M-Missiles are shoulder weapons for Skells in . They can be obtained from MG068: Megisia or by destroying Seidrs' weapon appendages.

Lindwurm Krasts (Japanese: , Rintovurumu Kurasuto) are three quest-exclusive enemies in . They are round-helmeted members of Lindwurm that are fought at level 66 at the entrance to the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago during Bana's Revenge.

Lindwurm (Japanese: , Rintovurumu) is an organization and family of enemies in . They are terrorists aiming to bring down the Empire of Mor Ardain using any means necessary. They seem to be affiliated with the Brionac, who have similar goals. Their members comprise mostly of Ardainian soldiers, but they also have some Titan weapons, attack dogs, and Drivers. Most of them are found at Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago, although some are found elsewhere during certain quests.

Lindwurm Sliders (Japanese: , Rintovurumu Suraidā) are quest-exclusive enemies in . They are fighter plane-like weaponized Titans used by Lindwurm that are fought at level 67 at the entrance to the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago during Bana's Revenge.
Lush Moonbeam Masks are Art Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Talmye Antiques in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Lost and Found is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya by speaking to Gronya, who stands by the ladder near Old Valantia, when the nation has at least 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Expeditionist" and "Water Mastery" Field Skills.

Lunch of Love is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist", "Leaping" and "Mineralogy" Field Skills.

Lost Property is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Leftherian Archipelago, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Focus" and "Kind Soul" Field Skills.

Longing for Mòrag is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain by talking to Fadhail at Port Anangham, when the nation has at least 3 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 80 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 20 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Water Mastery", "Dark Mastery" and "Fire Mastery" Field Skills.

Lindwurm Sollmeyers (Japanese: , Rintovurumu Zorumaiya) are enemies in . They are Lindwurm Titans, and can be found at level 44-46 at the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago. Four of them must be defeated to unlock Nim's level 3 Wild Grappler on her affinity chart.
Lindwurm Steins (Japanese: , Rintovurumu Sutain) are enemies in . They are members of Lindwurm, and can be found at level 40-45 at the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago.
Lindwurm Müllers (Japanese: , Rintovurumu Myūā) are enemies in . They are Ardainian members of Lindwurm, and can be found at level 41-44 at the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Long-Awaited Work (Japanese: , Taibō no Shinsaku) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 40 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 10 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist" and "Dark Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Fruity Rice Ball in Honeycomb Sweets * Adventures of Myram in Reedirait Bookstore

Local Pop Star? is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province during the Blade Quest Bearing Her Soul, after Ursula obtains 1,000 fans. The time required to complete this mission is 20 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 5 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Electric Mastery" and "Ice Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards stamps that are necessary to level up Ursula's attributes. It also increases Ursula's fanbase by a significant amount.

Lucky Monsters (Japanese: , rakkīmonsutā) are enemies in . They are as strong as normal monsters, but provide better items upon defeat or when performing a successful Burst Combo. More specifically, Lucky Monsters always drop items with a Rare or Legendary rarity. Normal items never drop. The number of items does not change compared to non-Lucky Monsters. Elite and Unique Monsters can also be Lucky Monsters as well. The probability of encountering a Lucky Monster is affected by the Shiny Hunter Affinity Bonus, which increases the odds by 1-10%.

The Lost Numbers Dormitory (Japanese: , Rosuto Nanbāzu Shukusha) is a Location in . It is located in the City. The left room on the ground floor becomes accessible during the Hero Quest Inhumanity. The room to the right becomes accessible by using the Homecomers' Key, which is obtained by completing the quest The Key to a New Home. Inside the right room, there is a Thank-You Card on the bed.

Lubon Quarmus are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Quarmu family, and can be found at level 44 in Erythia Sea. One is also fought at level 52 during the second wave of the Challenge Battle Ocean Day Parade.

Lubon Quarduns are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Quardun family, and can be found at level 46 in Erythia Sea. One is also fought at level 52 during the second wave of the Challenge Battle Ocean Day Parade.

Lottie is an NPC in . She is a Liberators soldier from the City who can be found around Colony 9's Command Center in Yesterdale. Lottie's Community is gained when talking to her after completing the quest Instructor Panacea, completing Chapter 3, and then talking with her twice.

Lui is an NPC in . She is a Liberators soldier from the City who can be found around Colony 9's Command Center in Yesterdale. Lui's Community is gained when talking to her after completing the quest Instructor Panacea and then talking with her twice.

Loneliness is a track from and , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track thirteen of disc four from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track thirteen of disc nine from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It uses motifs from Counterattack. This song plays during the following moments in : * When Azurda reverts to his larval state after taking heavy damage from the Monoceros. * Nia's talk with Vandham about her history with Torna. * Rex's talk with Pyra about her power after Vandham's funeral. * When Muimui tells the party about how Professor Soosoo was supposedly killed and how Professor Tatazo is still missing. * Rex and Nia's conversation with Fan la Norne about her missin

Makna Forest (Japanese: , Makuna Genseirin, lit. Makuna Primeval Forest, alt. Macuna Woods; English dub: ) is a jungle area visited by Shulk and friends in . A very hot and humid region, Makna Forest is located on Bionis' upper back, and is the home region of the Nopon. From Satorl Marsh, located on the Bionis' waist, the Forest can be reached on foot by passing through some of the Bionis' Interior's passages. The main village is the sole Nopon village on Bionis, Frontier Village, constructed inside the forest's biggest tree. Valak Mountain, located on Bionis's right arm, can also be accessed through Makna Forest. High above in the sky of Makna Forest, above even the clouds, is the Eryth Sea

Machina Cannons (Japanese: , Makina Kyanon) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are rifles that Sharla can wield that has the ability to damage Mechon. They can be acquired by purchasing them at Central Tower Shop in Agniratha for 34,320 G.
Machina Snipers (Japanese: , Makina Sunaipu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles that has the ability to damage Mechon. They are rifles wielded by Sharla.
Machina Biter III (Japanese: , Makina Kamukamu 3) is one of Riki's Biters, with the ability to damage Mechon. It can be acquired by purchasing it at Hidden Village Shop 1 on Fallen Arm for 37,800 G.

The Machina Nibbler II (Japanese: , Makina Bakubaku 2) is one of Riki's Biters, with the ability to damage Mechon. It is a direct upgrade of the Machina Nibbler, and presumably a downgrade of the Machina Nibbler III, although it has a higher physical defence, ether defence and block rate compared to III.
Machina Nibbler (Japanese: , Makina Bakubaku) is one of Riki's Biters, with the ability to damage Mechon. Machina Nibbler II is its direct upgrade.

Magic Stones are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Deinos in Makna Forest and can be traded for in Frontier Village. According to their description, they are rocks that emits weird light and contain strong ether. Two of them are needed for Material Quest 1 in Frontier Village.

Majestic Clone Barg (Japanese: , Ifū no Kuron Bōku) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Barg family, and can be found at level 77 in the Second Sanctum of Prison Island. It is significantly larger than other Bargs.

Marmor Apis (Japanese: , Marumoru Apisu) are flying insect enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Apis family, and can be found at level 40 in extreme heat or at night ouside of King Agni's Tomb in Makna Forest. They can drop the Royal Apis Nectar needed for one route of Popularity Premonition.

The M96 Crisis Unit (Japanese: , Kinkyū Bōei-gata Kyūjūrokushiki) is a quest exclusive Mechon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found in the Central Factory in the Mechon Factory. It appears during Daring Assault, and must be defeated, along with two Crisis Response Units, to complete Daring Assault. It can drop the Reinforced Thrusters needed for A Weapon Just For Me. All three respawn after completing the quest. By using its art Soaked Wall during the fight, the M96 Crisis Unit can call in reinforcements other Mechon around, or it may summon two others Crisis Response Units but with low probability.

no9=MONOX is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X, composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track nine of disc one from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack, and the ninth part of the suite titled 0rCH-SUITE "X". This music serves as the title screen (and menu) music for the game. The track also plays when the player completes The Skell License and obtains their first Skell, as well as when Lin manages to create a successful prototype for the Flight Module in A Girl's Wings.

Manami Kiyota (Japanese: , Kiyota Manami) is a music composer, arranger, lyricist, and performer. She has been active in the Japanese music industry since 2002 when she formed the band "YUENA" with a friend from university. Aside from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack, her work, which is most notable in the west, is as a vocalist and lyricist on Final Fantasy Song Book: mahoroba and as arranger on the song Destroyed Skyworld from the Super Smash Bros. soundtrack.

Marnuck Ruffians (Japanese: , Marunāku Rafian) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion troopers, and can be found at level 31-34 or at level 40 at Hilal Stronghold, Badr Stronghold, and at the southern foot of the Delusian Mountains below FN Site 419 in Sylvalum.
Machine Rook Quos (Japanese: , Mashīnrūku Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos and can be found at level 39 at the Lower Delusian Mountains in Sylvalum.
Magical Finding Rods (Japanese: , Hirameki Uranaibō) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found around the entrance of Oblivia. Two are needed during Mayhem.

Marnuck Loaders (Japanese: , Marunāku Rōdā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Marnuck Ganglion and can be found at level 33-40 in Sylvalum at Hilal Stronghold, under the broken land bridge west of FN Site 412, and in the middle of a group of Lutetia Petramands at the foot of the Delusian mountains south of FN Site 419. Six of them must be defeated during Law and Orders.
Maiden's Guardian Stars (Japanese: , Otome no Shugoboshi) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in cave areas around Oblivia, such as Rooney Cavern.

Machine Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Sakuraba Industries Gatling Gun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Flora category of the Noctilum Collectopedia. The Machine weapons available in-game are: * Storm Machine * Soldier Machine * Warrior Machine * Ophidian Machine * Destroyer Machine * Striker Machine * Delta Machine * Cosmic Machine * Nebulan Machine

Machine II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Sakuraba Industries Gatling Gun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Relics category of the Oblivia Collectopedia. The Machine II weapons available in-game are: * Storm Machine II * Soldier Machine II * Warrior Machine II * Ophidian Machine II * Destroyer Machine II * Striker Machine II * Delta Machine II * Cosmic Machine II * Nebulan Machine II

The Maelstrom (Japanese: , Uzushio) is a location in . It is a Titan ship docked on the Goldmouth Exit Dock in northern Goldmouth of the Argentum Trade Guild. It consists of a Salvaging vessel carried from above by a moderately sized fish-like Titan, and two smaller Titans docked into the rear of the ship that act as flying cranes for salvaging. The ship proper is only accessible after the events of Chapter 1, but it is possible to "discover" the ship before then by standing right in front of the gated boarding area. A salvage point can be found on the middle level of the ship.

Man-Eating Glenn (Japanese: , Hitogui no Doran) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Griffox family and can be found at level 32 at the Jelidorend Highlands, southwest of the Mine Elevator on the Upper Level of the Empire of Mor Ardain. It must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 3 "Superstrength" Affinity Reward.
Marrins (Japanese: , Mārin) are a family of enemies in the . They are flying fish-like creatures, similar to Serpronds.
Magic Canvases are Treasure items in . They can be obtained in the Empire of Mor Ardain through Salvaging at Port Anangham or Jarlin, Wing Area #1.

Margl Krabbles (Japanese: , Mūgo Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family and can be found at level 4-5 through Salvaging at Torigoth in the Gormott Province or on the Goldmouth Flight Deck of the Argentum Trade Guild during the quest Bana's Secret Treasure.

Mannam Juice Delivery (Japanese: , Manhonjūsu no Unpan) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province by talking to Motty in the entrance to Torigoth Market, when the nation has at least 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Entomology" and "Forestry" Field Skills.
The Maanus Driver (Japanese: , Mānasu Doraibā) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . He is a Driver enemy fought at level 37 on the Training Ground in the Kingdom of Uraya during A Test of Strength.

Magical Pink Pandoria (Japanese: ) is a DLC Aux Core in . It increases damage dealt by 50% when the Affinity between Driver and Blade is at max. It also changes Pandoria appearance when she equips the core, granting her a pink color scheme. It is unlocked after the Nopon Invitation is collected from the Helpful New Features released as part of the version 1.5.1 update and can be purchased at the Noponstone Exchange for 150 Noponstones in the Land of Challenge. The Mermaid-Blue Pandoria DLC Aux Core has an equivalent effect, which is functionally identical to the Affinity MAX Atk V Aux Core. The Devoted Marigold Nia DLC Aux Core has a stronger version of this equipment's effect.

He is an Ardainian Soldier who acted as a spy for Coeia, and can initially be found on the Ardainian flagship moored at Lascham Cove on Gormott alongside Yrrith. Both accompany the party to the Aletta Region, where they remain stationed at Aletta: Militia Garrison. During Duplicity, Yrrith sends the party out to find MacNeth, who has gone missing. He can be found in one of the abandoned houses in Hyber Village. Marga's Weeping (Japanese: , Maruga no Hirui) is a landmark in . It is a glowing blue obelisk located on the Bionis' Shoulder within Zekr Marga Quarry, directly before a room full of Telethia statues like those on Prison Island and a wind ether crystal deposit which must be visited to gain the High Ether Crystal during The Quest for High Ether.

The Malevolent Hollow (Japanese: , Janen no Kūdō) is a Landmark in . It is a cave located beyond the Brasa Geothermal Belt in Erythia Sea. The party's Ouroboros powers are restricted here, which prevents Interlinking. The cave is filled with very high level enemies.
Manegal is an NPC in . She is a Tantalese who can be found at Soprac Old Market in the Kingdom of Tantal during Fly in the Ointment.

It is track one of disc one from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack, Xenoblade Definitive Edition Original Soundtrack, and Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box, and track 1 on the Xenoblade Chronicles Special Soundtrack. This music serves as the Title Screen (and menu) music for the game. Outside of that, it plays in only one cutscene, specifically when Face Nemesis is unmasked as Fiora at Prison Island, revealing to Shulk and his companions that she was alive all along. Mechon M31 are flying Mechon enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles that appear only during the Mechon raid in Colony 9. They are Sight enemies and will attack if the party enters their detection range. They appear at level 5 in the Commercial, Residential, and Military Districts, and just outside the Main Entrance in Colony 9 during the Mechon raid. Contrary to the Story Exclusive Mechon M31, they will respawn, but only during the Mechon raid on Colony 9, and they drop a Treasure Chest. They are defeated and driven off along with the others when Metal Face flees.

Mechon Carriers are flying Vehicles in . They are mainly used to dispatch other Mechon troops. They firstly and occasionally appear in cutscenes and the background, for example during the Battle of Sword Valley. Later several ones can be viewed and approached while parked by two on each side of a dedicated access platform in the southern part of Sword Valley, near and along Galahad Fortress, south of the Fortress Rear Entrance, for example all around the Radio Tower.

The Mechon M64X is a story exclusive Mechon in . It is an enhanced "elite" versions of the standard Mechon M64. The Mechon M64X appears at level 22 at Freight Road in Colony 6, during the battle that takes place immediately after escaping the Ether Mine. During this battle, the Mechon M64X is a Kindred Enemy fought along with one Mechon M69X and two Mechon M53X. This Mechon does not respawn and does not drop Treasure Chests, although it does carry items. These items are unobtainable, however, as the Mechon M64X appears before Riki joins the party, and Riki's Yoink! ability is the only way to obtain items which enemies carry but do not drop. There is another normal variant of the Mechon M64X.

Masterful Gigapur (Japanese: , Shiden no Gigasuparu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Laia family, and can be found at level 77 on Travalga Bridge on Prison Island with a flock of Newgate Laias.

Medium Skeeters (Japanese: , Midoru Sukīto, Middle Skeeter) are mosquito-like enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Skeeter family, and can be found in Tephra Cave flying above a ledge above the Spring of Grief. They can drop Black Nectar, which is required for Education-Minded Suzanna.

The Mechon M69X (Japanese: , Rokujūkyūshiki Kishinhei: Kai) is a story exclusive Mechon in . Despite its name, it has the same appearance as a Mechon M72. It can be found at level 23 at Freight Road in Colony 6, during the battle that takes place immediately after escaping the Ether Mine. During this battle, the Mechon M69X is a Kindred Enemy fought along with one Mechon M64X and two Mechon M53X. It does not respawn nor drop Treasure Chests, although it does carry items. These items are unobtainable, however, as the Mechon M69X appears before Riki joins the party, and Riki's Yoink! ability is the only way to obtain items which enemies carry but do not drop.

Master Obart (Japanese: , Masutā Hobāto) is a boss in . It is also quest exclusive to the Chase Dickson Story Quest. It is a member of the Obart family, and can be found at level 78 at the Arena in Prison Island.
